paper.title: A Characterization of List Language Identification in the Limit
paper.summary: Characterizes list identification in the limit by a recursive k-Angluin condition, derives a decomposition into k ordinarily identifiable subcollections, and establishes optimal statistical-rate behavior.

formalization_scope.summary: The deterministic list-identification model, recursive k-Angluin condition, Algorithm 1, stabilization argument, Theorems 6 and 7, and headline Theorems 1 and 2 are formalized. Statistical Theorem 3 and Sections 8--10 are unformalized.
specializations: The countable collection is represented as an explicit indexed family F : Nat -> Set alpha, preserving duplicate indices for extensionally equal languages.

Generic headline wrappers assume an exact positive presentation for every indexed language; on the canonical Nat universe the source's nonempty-language assumption supplies these presentations automatically.
The lower bound proves the direct necessity implication using behavioral locking and induction on list width rather than formalizing the source's Algorithm 2 as an executable state machine.
The development is classical semantic mathematics and makes no computability or running-time claim, matching the source's stated existence-only focus.
gaps: Valid full-support distributions, statistical rate functions, randomized list identifiers, Top-k aggregation, and the exponential/no-vanishing-rate conclusions of Theorem 3 are not formalized.
Algorithm 2 is represented by a proof-equivalent behavioral-locking induction rather than a source-syntax state-machine implementation.
No P14 claim currently has a human statement-correspondence audit.

audit_refs.scope: Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the two P14 headline wrappers with Lean coverage.

claim_inventory.scope_description: The three headline results stated in Section 1.1: deterministic characterization Theorem 1, stratification Theorem 2, and statistical-rates Theorem 3.
exclusions: Definitions 1--6, equations (4)--(6), Claims 5.1 and 9.1, Algorithms 1--3, detailed Theorems 6--13, remarks, proof equations, and proof-only invariants are documented in the PaperMap rather than separate headline claim cards.
Computational complexity is outside the source's list-identifier model and outside this inventory.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means all three headline theorem groups are registered, not that every numbered source item is formalized.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: The two stable Results/Overview endpoints covering deterministic headline Theorems 1 and 2.
exclusions: Theorem 3 has no Lean endpoint because its statistical and probabilistic infrastructure is not formalized.

Canonical proof declarations for Theorems 6 and 7, Algorithm 1, Psi, stabilization, locking, and stratification internals are represented by the headline wrappers and documented in the PaperMap rather than duplicated as headline links.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: The linked declarations are exposed through GenLimit.ListIdentification.Results; complete is relative to this two-endpoint claim-linked scope.

claims.title: Characterization of k-list identification
claims.statement_summary: A countable indexed collection of nonempty languages is k-list identifiable in the limit if and only if every indexed language satisfies the recursive k-Angluin finite-tell-tale condition.

source_assessment.notes: Lean combines the source's detailed upper and lower bounds and preserves behavioral correctness up to extensionally equal family indices.

formalization.notes: The Overview wrapper delegates to the canonical equivalence assembled from formal Theorems 6 and 7.

lean_links.notes: Explicit presentability is the proof-relevant replacement for the source's countable-universe and nonempty-language assumptions.

relations.notes: The recursive characterization supplies the peeling construction used for stratification.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for Theorem 1.

claims.title: Stratification of k-list identifiable collections
claims.statement_summary: A countable language collection is k-list identifiable in the limit if and only if it is a union of k subcollections that are each ordinarily identifiable in the limit.

source_assessment.notes: Lean packages each subcollection as a set of family indices satisfying Angluin's condition relative to that layer. Under the explicit presentability hypothesis, the supplied relative learner proves ordinary identification on every layer.

formalization.notes: The Overview wrapper delegates to the peeling construction and the layerwise list identifier.

lean_links.notes: Layers are index sets, need not be disjoint, and may repeat or be empty, matching the source's union-of-k formulation.

relations.notes: The forward direction first obtains the k-Angluin condition and then peels k relative-Angluin layers.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for Theorem 2.

claims.title: Statistical rates for k-list identification
claims.statement_summary: A k-list identifiable collection admits an optimal exponential statistical identification rate, whereas a collection that is not k-list identifiable admits no rate tending to zero.

source_assessment.notes: The source's rate theorem is recorded but its probabilistic infrastructure has not been reviewed or formalized in Lean.

formalization.notes: Lean currently has no P14 valid-distribution/rate model, probabilistic list identifier, Top-k aggregation bridge, or exponential-rate proof.

relations.notes: The exponential upper bound uses stratification, while the no-rate direction transfers failure of deterministic k-list identification to the probabilistic setting.
